title: First-Class Relationships as a Representation Threshold: Identity, Time, Confidence, and Causation
abstract: arXiv:2603.13603v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Operational records -- who may access what, what changed, what caused an incident -- consist of relationships that involve several parties, hold for a period, are believed with some confidence, and cause one another. We ask what a representation must provide to store such records directly. We state four storage requirements: n-ary relationships with attributes, temporal validity, confidence with an evidential basis, and causal links between relationships. Under our definitions, each requires relationships to have identity: every relationship is stored, fetched and queried as an object with its own key. Confidence with an evidential basis and causal links also require composition: any relationship can take part in another. With n-ary relationships, either one therefore requires first-class relationships, which are identified, carry attributes, and compose at every arity. Conversely, first-class relationships suffice for all four

translated_title: 作为表示阈值的一等关系：身份、时间、置信度与因果
translated_abstract: 操作性记录——谁可以访问什么、什么发生了变更、什么导致了某次事故——由涉及多方的关系组成，这些关系在一段时间内有效、以某种置信度被相信，并且彼此之间存在因果联系。我们探究一个数据表示必须提供什么才能直接存储这类记录。我们提出了四个存储要求：带属性的 n 元关系、时间有效性、有证据支撑的置信度，以及关系之间的因果链接。在我们给出的定义下，每一项要求都需要关系具有身份：每个关系都作为一个拥有自己键的对象被存储、获取和查询。有证据支撑的置信度和因果链接还进一步要求可组合性：任何关系都可以参与构成另一个关系。对于 n 元关系而言，这两项要求中的任意一项都因此需要“一等关系”——即被唯一标识、携带属性、并在任意元数下都可组合的关系。反过来，一等关系本身也足以满足全部四项要求。
tldr: 该论文提出操作性记录的四个存储要求（带属性的 n 元关系、时间有效性、有证据的置信度、因果链接），并证明这些要求构成一个表示阈值：只有具备身份、属性和组合性的“一等关系”才能满足全部要求。
